name: Viana do Castelo – Cabedelo
notes: Windiest spot in the north (summer nortada, often 25 kn): kite at the north end of Cabedelo behind the big breakwater (flat water) or ride the waves outside. Schools on the beach; some rocks in the water; busy in summer. Also: Caminha – Moledo (waves).

name: Esposende – Ofir
notes: Flat knee-deep lagoon in the Cávado estuary behind the Ofir sandspit: reached by boat only (school transfer from Esposende port), nature reserve; strong current and boat traffic at the river mouth. Waves on the sea side, over the dunes. Pin is the sea beach: the lagoon has no OSM element.

name: Murtosa – Ria de Aveiro
notes: Flat standing-depth lagoon at Praia do Bico (Murtosa), Clube Nortada school on site. Southerlies in winter blow onshore; summer thermal wind is strong, so small kites. Slippery mussel bed (wear shoes); power cable just downwind of the road launch in westerlies. Ankle deep at low tide.

name: Lagoa de Óbidos
notes: Flat, waist-deep lagoon; lighter wind (big kites). Guides report kiting closed in summer (about 15 Jun–15 Sep) near the mouth and in the north of the lagoon: then ride by the sailing school or at Bom Sucesso. Also: Peniche – Baleal (ocean). Summer ban reported by a guide only: no official text found.

name: Guincho
notes: Very strong nortada, waves, rocks in the middle of the bay: advanced riders.

name: Fonte da Telha
notes: Closest spot to Lisbon; all levels, lighter wind; very busy in summer. Also: São João da Caparica (same coast, further north).

name: Alcochete
notes: Flat, shallow water on the Tagus estuary across from Lisbon (Praia dos Moinhos); beginner friendly, school on site. Stones; mud flats at low tide; water quality varies.

name: Lagoa de Albufeira
notes: Flat-water lagoon behind the sandbar; too shallow at low tide and in dry summers, deeper on the east side.

name: Lagos – Meia Praia
notes: Long sandy bay with schools on the beach; waves can build.

name: Alvor
notes: Ria de Alvor: flat, mostly waist-deep lagoon; launch on the sandspit by the dunes (dirt track from Alvor village). NW thermal, gusty near the edges; water from mid tide, some current.

name: Praia de Faro
notes: Ilha de Faro: waves on the ocean, flat water in the Ria Formosa (tide matters). The Faro maritime authority has restricted kiting in the Ria Formosa before: check local rules. Also: Fuseta, Cabanas de Tavira.

name: Manta Rota
notes: Long sandy beach in the east Algarve: SW thermal or E Levante, mostly flat to small waves; school (AlturaKites). Also: Cacela Velha.

name: Porto Santo
notes: 9 km beach; N wind is side-offshore and gusty in summer: experienced riders.

notes: Between two breakwaters, kiteable in both usual winds but few riders. Heavy shorebreak and strong currents at high tide in winter storms.
